name: GPS/WireOut
description: Ship navigated with GPS, but sampling device launched on a wire.

name: DVL/USBL
description: Real-time DVL dead-reckoning navigation supplemented with USBL.

name: DVL/LBL:Renav
description: Post-processed to merge DVL with LBL navigation.  When combined with LBL navigation, precision depth measurements, and gyrocompass attitude data, DVL navigation can result in vehicle positioning accuracy ranging from <1 meter to 10s of meters depending on deployment geometry and conditions, and the nature of the post-processing [Kinsey and Whitcomb, 2004, 2006; Ferrini et al., 2005; Kinsey et al., 2006; Ferrini et al., 2007].  **Note that sample position information derived from this navigation product MUST be manually verified (e.g. with bottom photos) to ensure the success of navigational post-processing.**

description: LOng RAnge Navigation

name: DGPS
description: Differential GPS

name: USBL
description: Ultra-Short Baseline

name: GLONASS
description: Global Navigation Satellite System

name: ACOUSTIC_RANGING/GPS
description: Acoustic ranging from a GPS-navigated ship to identify the location of instrumentation on the seafloor.

name: DVL:Renav:Confirmed
description: Indicates that the DVL:Renav positions have been confirmed by human inspection.

name: DVL/USBL:Renav
description: Post-processed to merge Doppler Velocity Log (DVL) with Ultra-Short BaseLine (USBL) navigation.

name: Locale
description: Position substituted from neighboring physiographic feature or deployed instrument.

name: LAYBACK
description: Layback navigation is typically calculated based on (1) the ship's GPS coordinates, (2) the amount of wire out to the towed platform, (3) the water depth of the platform (if available).

name: GPS
description: Global Positioning System

name: GPS:Assumed
description: GPS was available and has been assumed to be the source of navigational information.

name: RTK GPS
description: Real-Time Kinematic GPS

name: LBL
description: Real-time Long BaseLine navigation [Hunt et al., 1974; Milne, 1983].  Utilizes travel times from acoustic transponders deployed near the seafloor to calculate positional information.  Motion of the transponders, which are typically deployed on long tethers (up to 600 m in high relief terrain), result in motion of the reference frame, introducting positioning uncertainties on the order of meters.

name: DVL/LBL:Renav:Confirmed
description: Indicates that the DVL/LBL:Renav positions have been confirmed by human inspection.

name: DVL/LBL/INS
description: Real-time DVL dead-reckoning navigation supplemented with LBL navigation and INS (Inertial Navigation System) navigation.

name: DVL
description: Doppler Velocity Log

name: DVL:Renav
description: DVL data post-processed to remove obvious errors in Doppler position data. Errors on the order of 10s of meters are likely to exist in these data and are due to the limitations of dead-reckoning navigation with DVL sonars.  Users should refer to bottom photos to verify positioning information.

name: LAYBACK/LBL
description: Layback navigation supplemented with LBL

name: DVL/LBL
description: Real-time DVL dead-reckoning navigation supplemented with LBL navigation to help constrain fixes to a geographic coordinate system.  Errors on the order of 10s (sometimes 100s) of meters are likely in these data.

name: Not Applicable
description: Not applicable
